paraphrase: Nirvāṇa is not an existent, for then it would have the marks of old age and death, would be conditioned and would depend on grasping; nor is it a non-existent, for where there is no existent there is no non-existent, and nirvāṇa does not exist in dependence.

paraphrase: Obscured by ignorance one forms the threefold formations that lead to rebirth and by these actions goes to a destiny; consciousness conditioned by the formations enters that destiny; name-and-form is infused; the six sense-bases arise; contact; feeling; craving for feeling; the fourfold grasping; becoming; birth; and from birth old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, dejection and despair — thus arises this whole mass of suffering.
